clue.text: Workers possibly having loud arguments

indicators.note: having means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: worker bees, so bees are workers of a kind
F is forte, the musical term for loud

explanation.surface: Employees are pictured having noisy rows at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Workers' are worker bees here, not people in an office.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaints or grievances aired angrily are called beefs in informal speech.

clue.text: Sourdough and ciabatta maybe soak up most of the spreads

indicators.note: to soak up is to absorb, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: sourdough and ciabatta are examples of breads

indicators.note: most of drops the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Bread mops up most of the butter and jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreads' looks like butter and jam but is the noun for widths.
explanation.definitionFit: Widths or extents, how far things spread across, are measures of breadth.

clue.text: Praise once given out about one parent

indicators.note: given out as in distributed, so the letters are scattered and reordered
about means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: mum is a mother, a parent
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Compliments were once handed out about a mother or father.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal speech or piece of writing lavishing praise on someone is a eulogy or tribute.

clue.text: Father is around and about

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: RE means concerning or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A dad is out and about.
explanation.definitionFit: To father offspring, especially of animals, is to beget them.

clue.text: Outlandish skits are s***!

indicators.note: outlandish means bizarre, so these letters are put into a strange new order

parts.note: only the opening s is a letter; the rest are symbols standing in for the hidden word

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses some bizarre comedy sketches with a censored expletive.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: the starred-out swearword is itself spelt with the symbols in question.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed star symbols are what a newspaper uses to blank out the letters of a rude word.

clue.text: Do Aussie parliamentarians exert influence here?

definitions.meaning: to do is to perform or take action
the Australian Capital Territory, home to Canberra and the federal parliament

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether Australian politicians wield power in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation is for the Australian Capital Territory, where Canberra and Parliament House are.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something is to take action; the territory abbreviation names where Australia's federal lawmakers sit.

clue.text: After the start of treatment, osteopaths supply products containing calcium

indicators.note: start of takes the opening letter
supply read as supple, bending the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Once treatment begins, bone therapists provide calcium supplements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' reads as 'provide' but signals the letters are reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Many dental pastes contain calcium compounds as a mild abrasive, so they fit the description.

clue.text: Some footballers are left to roam, crazy and free

indicators.note: to roam is to wander, so the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: mad and crazy are synonyms
to rid is to free of something

explanation.surface: Some players are given licence to wander, wild and unrestrained.
explanation.definitionFit: The Madrid club is a famous Spanish football team, a group of footballers.

clue.text: Untidy front of station and waiting area

indicators.note: front of takes the opening letter

parts.note: a lobby is an entrance hall where people wait

explanation.surface: The entrance of a station and its waiting room are messy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy and lazy in appearance, like a slob, means messy.

clue.text: Precious metal one extracted for a plate

indicators.note: one letter is taken out and another put in its place

parts.note: silver is a precious metal
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Valuable metal is mined to make a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat serving tray, often of silver, is a kind of plate.

clue.text: Without reading, perhaps, save newspaper clipping

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: save in the sense of but or apart from
reading is one of the three Rs of basic schooling

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a press cutting without bothering to read it.
explanation.definitionFit: A short passage cut or quoted from a longer text, such as a news story, is an extract.

clue.text: Retired councillor — a non-gambler — keeps having repeated wins

indicators.note: Retired says the hidden letters are read backwards
keeps means holds inside, so the letters are held within these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A retired local politician who never bets nonetheless keeps winning.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave no word to signal the hidden letters; 'keeps' does that job, so the definition starts at 'having'. 'Retired' sends the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a streak of success, one victory following another.

clue.text: Extremely divisive way of doing things elicits protest

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the outermost letters of the word

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a method of working

explanation.surface: A deeply polarising approach provokes a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A street march or rally against something is a demonstration, shortened in everyday speech.

clue.text: Bust of a meth lab is understandable

indicators.note: bust as in broken, so these letters are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A police raid on a drug laboratory is easy to make sense of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' reads as a police raid but signals the letters are broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be fathomed, grasped in depth, is comprehensible.

clue.text: Guy responsible for dynamite exploding near Blofeld

indicators.note: exploding blows the letters apart and reassembles them

explanation.surface: A man with dynamite blows up close to the Bond villain Blofeld.
explanation.walkthrough: Blofeld is the Bond villain, fitting the explosive theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish chemist who founded the Nobel Prizes invented dynamite in 1867.

clue.text: It could be messier, so — to begin with — let's keep it simple!

indicators.note: to begin with takes the opening letter
it could be signals that the letters may form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone advises keeping things simple, since they could get messier.
explanation.definitionFit: The minimalist motto says restraint and simplicity achieve more than excess.

clue.text: Cash used for old, decrepit building that might fall over

indicators.note: decrepit means worn out and falling apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Money was spent on an ancient, rundown building that may collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower of propped playing cards is notoriously unstable, and the phrase describes any shaky scheme.

clue.text: Donations bound to form part of most museums?

parts.note: donations and gifts are synonyms
to bound is to jump or hop

explanation.surface: Donations are sure to make up part of most museums' collections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'certain' but means a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Most museums have a store selling souvenirs near the exit, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Quiz programme essentially needs two good captains

indicators.note: essentially points to the heart, the central letter

parts.note: G is good, so two of them
heads are leaders, like captains

explanation.surface: A quiz show really needs two strong team leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: A BBC television quiz pits a team of brainy champions against challengers.

clue.text: Learning through study is sure to stop when one starts to need guidance

indicators.note: to stop as in plug a hole, so one piece fills a gap in the other

parts.note: as in the sense of while or when
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: starts takes the opening letter of each following word

parts.note: sure and certain are synonyms

explanation.surface: A student says self-study will cease the moment one needs a teacher's help.
explanation.walkthrough: CERTAIN plugs the gap in AS + I + NG, the starts of 'need guidance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Finding something out for certain by investigation is establishing it, a synonym of discovering.

clue.text: Pretentious greeting omitting names

indicators.note: omitting means leaving out, so letters are removed

parts.note: chin-chin is a toast or greeting when drinking
N is the abbreviation for name, so two of them

explanation.surface: An affected hello leaves out people's names.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy and affectedly refined, a style trying too hard to be elegant.

clue.text: Crew rightly reported an incompetent hotel worker

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the sound of the words gives the letters

parts.note: to crew is to man; rightly is well

explanation.surface: The crew are said to have correctly reported a hopeless hotel employee.
explanation.walkthrough: Manuel is the bumbling Spanish waiter in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers.
explanation.definitionFit: The hapless waiter in the classic sitcom set in a Torquay hotel is the character meant.

clue.text: House by headland embodying a rushed, oddly rough quality

indicators.note: embodying means containing within, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: a ness is a promontory, as in Loch Ness or place names like Sheerness

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A seaside house has a hurried, uneven feel about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' and 'headland' are both abbreviated pieces, not the definition; a ness is a headland, as in Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasping, rough voice is the defining trait described here, a gruff huskiness.

clue.text: Irritation starts to concern him after sex

indicators.note: after places the following letters behind the first piece

parts.note: IT is a long-standing slang word for sex appeal or sex

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: A man's unease begins to show once intercourse is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A tickling urge to scratch is a minor skin irritation.

clue.text: Staff involved in producing I'm A Celebrity

indicators.note: the letters are involved within the following words

explanation.surface: Crew members work on the reality TV show I'm A Celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: I'm A Celebrity is a British reality TV show set in the jungle.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial staff of office, or a medieval club, is a mace.

clue.text: Joule appears endlessly during search for physicist

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

indicators.note: endlessly drops both ends of the word, keeping the middle

explanation.surface: A unit-named scientist turns up, incomplete, in a hunt for another physicist.
explanation.walkthrough: Joule is also a physicist, a red herring for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles-Augustin de Coulomb was the French scientist who gave his name to the unit of electric charge.

clue.text: Tense situation involving companion's money at one point

indicators.note: involving means containing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a tense situation is a drama
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A tense moment concerns a friend's cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek currency was this unit before the euro replaced it, so it was money once.

clue.text: I'm an idiot and party hard

parts.note: a do is a party
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone admits to stupidity and partying too hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer Simpson's exclamation admits a foolish blunder of one's own.

clue.text: One tiny bit of laudanum will finally cure the unending sickness

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a tiny bit is just the opening letter
finally takes the closing letter

parts.note: to cure is to heal

indicators.note: unending drops the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A single drop of opiate will at last cure a persistent illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor health and sickness are synonyms for being unwell.

clue.text: Old props regularly used for public displays

parts.note: EX means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, here the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Former theatre props are reused at exhibitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Large exhibitions or trade shows are known by this short form.
